title: Insurance, Indemnification and Bonding Posture: Operational Insurance Carriage on Inspection Programs, Station Bond/Proof-of-Insurance Verification, and Damage/Force-Majeure Restoration
capability_statement:
Parsons' available proposal evidence on this theme is operational and program-specific rather than a corporate-level statement of insurance scope, limits, and bonding capacity. On comparable Vehicle Inspection / I/M Programs, Parsons (a global, 18,000+-person company with 79 years of experience that entered the vehicle inspection industry in 1984) demonstrates four insurance-adjacent capabilities directly relevant to the contracting agency's R-005, R-018, R-019, R-020, R-021, A-019, R-040, and related indemnification requirements (chunk 1975).

First, Parsons carries and maintains general liability insurance covering damages or destruction at client facilities while fulfilling the contract; in the event damage or destruction occurs at a program facility, Parsons restores the premises to as nearly as possible their original condition and value, with the contracting agency's Project Manager retaining final approval on construction workmanship. Where damage results from force majeure, the contracting agency pays for repairs through its insurance carrier and reimburses Parsons; Parsons invoices the agency for the improvement costs but uses only enough funds from the insurance carrier to refurbish the site to its original value (chunks 4109, 4110).

Second, Parsons carries vehicle insurance for the oversight and covert audit fleets it operates on behalf of the contracting agency. On a comparable I/M Program, Parsons assumes responsibility for all applicable vehicle insurance, fuel, repairs, and other operating expenses for the oversight vehicles used in safety and emissions audits, and reimburses auditors using personal vehicles at the federal mileage rate (chunk 2263). Parsons explicitly provides covert vehicle insurance for both emissions covert and safety covert oversight activities, leveraging its own established covert vehicle dealership (set up with the assistance of the contracting agency's Department of State on a comparable program) that allows Parsons to purchase and sell vehicles at auction while protecting the identity of covert vehicles from purchase to decommissioning (chunks 2155, 2271).

Third, station bond and proof-of-insurance verification is built into Parsons' inspection-station audit procedures. As part of overt station audits performed under 40 CFR 51.363 and the contracting agency's regulations, Parsons' auditors check that each station has the proper bond or proof of insurance, alongside verification of inspector credentials, equipment, recordkeeping, sticker controls, and certificates posted at the station (chunks 2134, 2266). On the e-SAFETY inspection workflow, the system additionally maintains insurance-company name autofill for inspector data entry and flags or pops up inconsistencies such as expired insurance, prompting the inspector to confirm before continuing (chunks 2293, 2296).

Fourth, Parsons' Tab J (Certificate of Insurance) and Section 3.6 (Insurance Requirements) are explicitly addressed in its proposal table of contents on a comparable program (chunks 3602, 3612), indicating the standard practice of providing a Certificate of Insurance as a required submittal artifact, though the underlying coverage scope and limits are not contained in the chunks available for this synthesis.

The evidence base for this theme is materially thinner than for operational themes. None of the available chunks recite specific insurance limits (for example, the $1,000,000 combined-single-limit auto liability called out by R-019), workers' compensation/employers' liability scope (R-021), additional-insured endorsement language (R-020), cybersecurity liability coverage scope (A-019), surety bonding capacity, or indemnification language responsive to R-040 / A-087 / A-089 / A-098. The capture team must source these from corporate Risk Management, broker certificates, and prior compliant submittals - they are not represented in the proposal chunks available here.

named_past_performance.name: Comparable State I/M Program - Operational Insurance Carriage on a Vehicle Inspection / Emissions Program
named_past_performance.scope: Program and operations management of a state vehicle emissions inspection program for a State DOT/State Motor Vehicle agency, including general liability coverage for client-facility damage or destruction; vehicle insurance carriage for an overt and covert oversight fleet (with Parsons' own covert vehicle dealership for auction purchase/sale); station audit programs that verify station bond or proof of insurance under 40 CFR 51.363; and an e-SAFETY inspection workflow that flags expired insurance during data entry. Tab J (Certificate of Insurance) submitted as a required attachment.
named_past_performance.outcome: Parsons maintained general liability insurance for damages or destruction at program facilities; assumed responsibility for applicable vehicle insurance, fuel, repairs, and operating expenses for oversight and covert vehicles; verified station bond/proof of insurance during overt audits; and embedded expired-insurance validation in the e-SAFETY inspector workflow.

named_past_performance.name: Comparable State Vehicle Inspection / I/M Program - Covert Vehicle Insurance and Dealership Infrastructure
named_past_performance.scope: Operation of an emissions and safety covert audit infrastructure including covert vehicle purchase, insurance, decommissioning, and rotation, supported by a Parsons-owned covert vehicle dealership (established with the assistance of the contracting agency's Department of State) enabling Parsons to purchase and sell vehicles at auction while protecting covert vehicle identity from purchase to decommissioning.
named_past_performance.outcome: Parsons provides covert vehicle insurance and is the only vendor on a comparable program with the existing covert dealership infrastructure that protects the identity of covert vehicles end-to-end; covert vehicle reports including VIN, year, make, model, title number, odometer, and commission/decommission dates are delivered to the contracting agency monthly in electronic format.

differentiators: 1) Parsons-owned covert vehicle dealership (established with the agency's Department of State on a comparable I/M Program) that provides covert vehicle insurance and protects covert vehicle identity from purchase through decommissioning - cited in the comparable proposal as the only vendor with this existing infrastructure (chunks 2155, 2271). 2) Operational insurance carriage embedded in delivery: general liability for client-facility damage/destruction (chunk 4109), oversight-fleet vehicle insurance with federal-mileage reimbursement for personal-vehicle use (chunk 2263), and structured force-majeure restoration mechanics that route agency insurance proceeds back to site refurbishment (chunk 4110). 3) Built-in station bond/proof-of-insurance verification during overt I/M and safety audits, aligned to 40 CFR 51.363 (chunks 2134, 2266). 4) Insurance-aware inspection workflow - e-SAFETY autofill of carrier names and automated flag/popup on expired insurance during the inspector's data entry (chunks 2293, 2296).
gap_notes: Evidence base is materially thin for an 'Insurance & Bonding' theme - the available chunks describe operational insurance carriage on inspection programs and station-side bond/insurance verification, not corporate insurance scope, limits, or surety bonding capacity. The capture team must source the following from corporate Risk Management, the broker of record, and prior compliant submittals before this theme can be fully responsive: (a) Cybersecurity liability insurance scope and limits (RFP A-019, Section 30.4) - no chunk in this evidence set describes Parsons' cyber policy; (b) Commercial Auto Liability with $1,000,000 combined single limit and Additional Insured endorsement language (R-018, R-019, R-020, Section 4.2.b); (c) Workers' Compensation and Employers' Liability scope (R-021, Section 4.2.c); (d) Commercial General Liability limits and aggregates (R-005, Section 4.2) - chunk 4109 confirms general liability is maintained but does not state limits; (e) Indemnification clause acceptance and any exceptions for R-040, A-087, A-089 (encryption-failure breach indemnity), A-098 (indemnification in addition to insurance), and the related N.J. and Maryland indemnification provisions (V-001, V-005, A-020, A-021, R-001, R-004, R-036) - none of the available chunks contain Parsons' indemnification response language; (f) Surety bond / performance bond capacity, carriers, and prior bonding history; (g) Tab J Certificate of Insurance content - chunk 3612 confirms the Tab exists in the comparable submittal but the certificate itself is not in the chunk set; (h) Union/check-off indemnification clauses (A-012, A-021 union-related) - not addressed in any chunk; (i) Aetna HMO offset Appendix B reference (R-011) - appears to be a benefits/payroll item miscategorized into this theme and is not represented in the inspection-program evidence; (j) N.J.S.A. 52:32-60.1 Vendor / Russia-Belarus certification compliance (V-012) - not represented. The evidence is also fully state-neutralized but originates from the Pennsylvania (PennDOT 3522R12) Emissions and Maryland (V-HQ-24019-S) Vehicle Emissions Inspection Program submittals; no corporate dossier matches were available, which is the principal driver of the thinness.
